title: Identification and reporting of occupational diseases and detection mechanisms for imminent occupational diseases - a nationwide cross-sectional survey among German trauma surgeons authorised by the statutory accident insurance (Durchgangsärzte)
summary:
Some illnesses are caused by a person's work – for example joint damage after many years of heavy physical labour, or skin conditions caused by handling certain substances. These are known as occupational diseases.

Doctors in Germany are legally required to report it when they suspect that an illness is work-related. Only once such a report is made can the statutory accident insurance check whether the person is entitled to special treatment, preventive measures or compensation.

In everyday practice, however, such suspicions often go unreported or are reported late. Little research exists on why this happens.

In this study we therefore survey doctors who treat people after occupational accidents. We want to find out: what makes them notice in daily practice that an illness might be work-related? At what point during treatment does this become apparent? What keeps them from reporting a suspicion? And which early signs might help to detect an emerging occupational disease sooner, perhaps even in time to prevent it?

The survey is conducted online and takes about 10 to 15 minutes. Participation is voluntary and anonymous. No patient data are collected.

From the answers we aim to derive concrete proposals for detecting occupational diseases earlier and reporting them more reliably in future.
conditions: Occupational diseases as listed in the German Occupational Diseases Ordinance, in particular musculoskeletal occupational diseases, and imminent occupational diseases

interventions.name: Single-arm observation group: medically active persons in Germany who are involved in the statutory accident insurers' specialist treatment procedure (Durchgangsarztverfahren) and/or who treat patients covered by statutory accident insurance. Participants complete a structured, anonymous online ques

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Currently medically active in Germany
2. Involvement in the treatment of patients covered by statutory accident insurance
3. Willingness to participate in the survey
4. Sufficient knowledge of the German language
5. Minimum age of 18 years
Exclusion criteria:
1. No medical practice in Germany
2. No involvement in the care of patients covered by statutory accident insurance
3. No consent given at the start of the questionnaire
